links_touching_record.rationale: This measure is the source-grounded verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000006's validity-marking and envelope-check criteria, established from the pinned source's current-sensor receive callback and the SOA module's gating on the invalid flag. The link asserts coverage of two of the requirement's three criteria; the third, that no invalid measurement reaches any supervisory decision, needs a consumer census this measure does not contain.

The system requirement refines the stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000004 into a system-level obligation. The need is in stakeholder language and the requirement is measurable; the trace is the derivation step.

FB2-SW-SWR-000001 is the lower-level requirement allocated to the system requirement FB2-SYS-SYR-000006. The two statements and acceptance criteria were read against each other before the link was made, so the system requirement is covered indirectly through its allocation rather than directly by a measure of its own.

FB2-HW-TSR-000002 is the lower-level requirement allocated to the system requirement FB2-SYS-SYR-000006. The two statements and acceptance criteria were read against each other before the link was made, so the system requirement is covered indirectly through its allocation rather than directly by a measure of its own.
The calibration specification owns the current and temperature values the supervision requirement acquires.

asil_justification.open_item: The absence of a recorded derivation is a property of this corpus, not a demonstrated property of the product. If a future HARA were to identify a hazardous event on the current or temperature path, this requirement would have to be allocated to that goal and the marking here would be wrong. This field records the present state of the allocation and does not claim the absence is permanent.
asil_justification.reason: This requirement is classified 'interface'. It specifies acquisition, validity marking and plausibility comparison for measurement values; it does not itself specify a reaction to a hazardous event, and no safety goal in this corpus allocates the current and temperature paths to one. ISO 26262 allocates an ASIL to a requirement derived from a hazardous event of the safety goal, and there is no such derivation recorded here, so not_applicable is the schema's own enumerated value for that case.
asil_justification.scope_of_this_classification: This field records why safety_allocation.asil is not_applicable on this requirement. It is a statement about this record's own allocation bookkeeping inside a fictional reference project. It is not a determination about the real foxBMS 2 product, whose acquisition of pack current and cell temperature has never been allocated an ASIL by anyone.
what_this_does_not_assert: It does not assert conformity with ISO 26262, and it is not a certification, a type approval, or evidence of one. Nothing in this field was audited to produce it.

It does not assert human approval. human_approval_status on this record is pending, production_authorized is false and product_verification_credit is false, and no functional-safety expert has confirmed any of it.
It does not establish that any ASIL was correctly assigned to any safety requirement in this corpus. It explains only why this requirement is not itself an ASIL-allocated item.
It does not assert tool qualification. No tool used anywhere in this corpus has been qualified for a safety purpose.
It does not assert an ASPICE capability level for anything.

record_verbatim.rationale: The safety chain in this corpus is entirely a cell-voltage chain: the hazard, the safety goal and all four functional safety requirements concern cell voltage. Current and temperature supervision are system-level requirements nonetheless, because the item publishes charge and discharge limits that the converter is assumed to respect (FB2-ASM-003), and a limit published from an untrustworthy measurement is not a limit. This requirement is stated as a system requirement rather than a safety requirement precisely because the corpus carries no hazard, no safety goal and no ASIL for the current and temperature paths. Recording it as a system requirement with no ASIL is the honest position; inflating it to match the cell-voltage chain would be an unsupported ASIL assignment.

revision_history.description: System requirement authored because SYS.2 was recorded as a coverage gap with no system requirement record in either profile. System-level: it states what the integrated item must do and allocates to the existing technical requirements rather than restating them.

revision_history.description: Added the asil_justification that the requirement applicability validator requires and did not find: this record marks safety_allocation.asil as not_applicable, which requirement.schema.json enumerates as the value for a requirement to which no ASIL determination applies, and the rule requires a recorded reason for that marking. The reason had been present only inside safety_allocation.mitigation and safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref, which are required on every requirement whatever its marking and are therefore populated identically on the ASIL_D records; they cannot serve as a justification specific to this marking. The new field states the reason on its own, names what the safety_goal_ref trace does and does not carry, and records the open items where the marking depends on something not yet established. The asil value, the statement, the mitigation, the safety_goal_ref and the revision-relevant content of the record are unchanged. Remediation of the requirement applicability validator finding raised by finding FB2-REV-FND-000032. Nothing in this field asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.
